what: router load test run ON the router host (t4g.large, 2 vCPU) against localhost, scripts/aws_loadtest.py, 2026-10-15
source: table pasted by the user from scripts/aws_run.sh output (hand-copied; the raw JSONL stayed on the router in /tmp/loadtest.jsonl); runs/aws-loadtest.jsonl was saved with RAW=1 scripts/aws_run.sh (machine-logged, 7 records)

reading.latency_rule: latency is about in_flight / throughput (8 -> 2.0 s, 16 -> 4.2 s)
reading.cliff: 32 in flight: 320 of 320 failed at the router's 5 s encoder timeout; 16 in flight was fine (max 4.94 s)
reading.bottleneck: encoder CPU (router host CPU 69% at 1 in flight, 97-100% from 4)

predictions.errors_between_16_and_32: half right: none at 16, 100% at 32 (a cliff, not a slope)
predictions.shards_idle: not confirmed yet (EC2 CPU metric lags 5 minutes)

monitoring_blind_spot: failed searches had no timing in the router log line, so the latency chart under-reported during the overload; fixed in services/router/src/server.ts (total on every line)

second_invocation_after_overload.observed: a 7th record in runs/aws-loadtest.jsonl: a second run of the script started at concurrency 1 (40 requests): 15 errors, 0.42 req/s, p50 344.6 ms; it stopped itself (>20% errors)
second_invocation_after_overload.circumstances: time and reason NOT logged; the user was asked whether they re-ran the command
second_invocation_after_overload.hypothesis_unconfirmed: the encoder kept working through the roughly 320 requests the router had already given up on (no cancellation), so it was still saturated; a metastable failure. To be checked with Logs Insights on /genkart/encoder (requests per minute and slowest ms after the load stopped)
second_invocation_after_overload.possible_fix: router sends a deadline, the encoder drops requests nobody waits for; router limits in-flight searches and answers 'busy' quickly; then repeat the load test
